previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A middle-aged woman with type 1 diabetes, a history of two kidney transplants, and hypothyroidism was admitted for evaluation of atypical chest pain. She reported intermittent chest pressure radiating to the shoulder, associated with one episode of vomiting. Initial workup, including serial troponins and an exercise stress test, showed no evidence of acute myocardial infarction. The chest pain was ultimately deemed likely musculoskeletal. During the hospitalization, she was found to have a urinary tract infection caused by ciprofloxacin-resistant E. coli, confirmed by urine culture. She was treated with oral Macrobid, with resolution of fever and symptoms. Her immunosuppressive regimen was adjusted: cyclosporine was discontinued, and sirolimus dosing was modified. Her levothyroxine dose was reduced due to a low TSH level. Blood glucose levels were elevated, attributed to the infectious state, and managed in coordination with the diabetes team. She remained stable throughout her stay and was discharged home on a revised medication regimen with follow-up instructions.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ yo F with IDDM with complications, s/p renal transplant on 
immunosupressants who presents with multiple vague complaints 
and concern for worsening infection. Patient is on day 4 of 
antibiotics for a UTI. Those symptoms have gone but she 
developed hyperglycemia, low grade fevers to 99, abdominal 
cramping and diarrhea.
.
# UTI: Urinalysis was negative for evidence of infection, 
suggesting that antibiotics were effective.  Sensitivities on 
outpatient urine culture also suggest that cefpodoxime should 
cover her infection. She was afebrile and without leukocytosis.  
She was given one dose of broader spectrum IV ceftriaxone, after 
which she was switched back to cefpodoxime but at a higher dose. 
 She improved clinically. She was discharged with a total 14 day 
course of the higher dose.  Blood and urine cultures were 
negative to date at the time of discharge. 
.
# diarrhea/abdominal cramping: This was likely related to 
alteration of gut flora by antibiotics.  Her outpatient 
furosemide was held. 
.
# s/p kidney transplant: Renal function was at baseline.  
Prednisone, cellcept, and rapamune were continued, as was 
Bactrim prophylaxis.
.
# IDDM: Fingerstick blood glucose values were noted to be 
elevated into the 200s-300s.  She was given a diabetic diet.  
The cause of the hyperglycemia was thought to be infection.  She 
was on an insulin pump, and pump malfunction was considered, 
given that ___ were elevated despite appropriate treatment for 
the UTI.  The patient was offered a consultation from the ___ 
___, where she gets her outpatient care; however, 
she elected to be discharged prior to this, with plans to follow 
up as an outpatient.
.
# HTN: Home ACEI, beta blocker, and HCTZ were continued.  
Furosemide was held given diarrhea.  She was normotensive.  
.
# hyperlipidemia: ASA and statin were continued.
.
# PVD: Pletal was continued
.
# hypothyroidism: Levothyroxine was continued
.
# osteoporosis: Calcium/Vit D were continued
.
.
